PASSO 1: o imparfait é o cenário, o fund: STEP 1: the imparfait is the setting, the background of the picture: the time, the weather, feelings, habits. The passé composé is the event, the action that moves the story forward. STEP 2: «Il pleuvait (setting) quand je suis sorti (event).» STEP 3: actions that happen one after another: passé composé: «Je me suis levé, j'ai pris mon café et je suis parti.» STEP 4: an action in progress interrupted by another: imparfait + passé composé: «Je mangeais quand le téléphone a sonné.» STEP 5: two long simultaneous actions: imparfait + imparfait, with «pendant que»: «Il cuisinait pendant que je lisais.» STEP 6: event words: «soudain, tout à coup, un jour, ce jour-là, alors». Setting words: «toujours, souvent, d'habitude, pendant que, chaque jour». STEP 7: a limited action with a fixed duration: passé composé: «J'ai habité deux ans à Paris.» STEP 8: a prolonged state with no marked end: imparfait: «J'habitais à Paris.» STEP 9: the same verb changes meaning: «Je savais» (I knew) × «J'ai su» (I found out).
em português a diferença é a mesma entre: In English the same difference exists between «I spoke» (simple past) and «I was speaking / I used to speak» (imperfect). In French, the completed past is the «passé composé», a compound tense, not a simple one: «j'ai parlé». The trick is to ask: «is this setting or event?»

em português contamos histórias com «era: In English we tell stories with «once upon a time… suddenly…», alternating the past continuous and the simple past. French does the same and the logic is identical: setting in the imparfait, event in the passé composé, reaction back in the imparfait.

STEP 3: «pouvoir»: «Je pouvais venir» (I could) × «J'ai pu venir» (I managed to come). STEP 4: «vouloir»: «Je voulais partir» (I wanted to) × «J'ai voulu partir» (I tried, I decided to leave).
